claims.claim: Origen was born probably at Alexandria in 184/85 and died probably in Tyre in 253/54 after imprisonment and torture during the Decian persecution.
Origen was an outstanding theologian of the early Greek-speaking Church and an excellent teacher to whose lectures students flocked.

Origen's chief aim was to be an interpreter of the Scriptures, and to this end he composed scientific commentaries on various books of the Old and New Testaments, homilies, and short exegetical notes.

The translations presented belong to the category of homilies, and though Origen did not reject the literal sense of Scripture, he was more intent upon the spiritual meanings of passages selected from Genesis and Exodus.
The English translation was made from the surviving Latin translation of Rufinus of Aquileia.
The work includes Greek fragments of the Homilies on Genesis and Exodus.
The work contains a section on Rufinus' assumptions, methodology, and reliability as a translator.
Origen was the most important theologian and biblical scholar of the early Greek church, and his greatest work is the Hexapla.
Origen was born at Alexandria of Christian parents, and our chief source of information on his life is the sixth book of Eusebius' Ecclesiastical History.
Origen became a teacher with such success that he was recognized, first informally, then in 203 officially, as head of the school.
